headline: Deep learning tools for genome annotation are being systematically benchmarked
label: Genomic Deep Learning Benchmarks
summary: Recent preprints systematically evaluate DNA language models and deep learning predictors across scaffolding, coding sequence, and gene annotation tasks.
synthesis: These preprints share a focus on learned sequence representations and deep models for genome assembly and annotation, with evaluation central to each. SPA-C couples a compact CNN operating on local Hi-C contact matrices with a graph-solving step for genome scaffolding and reports outperforming four existing tools. The sORF study benchmarks seven traditional machine learning models using k-mer, Word2Vec, and genomic language model embeddings for cancer-associated small ORFs in non-coding RNA across 15 cancers. DeepCDS applies ESM-2 protein language model embeddings alongside nucleotide features to predict coding sequences in short prokaryotic reads. GENATATOR evaluates DNA language models for ab initio gene annotation, reporting that fine-tuning is required and proposing biologically grounded metrics and datasets. A recurring novelty is the emphasis on representation choice and biologically grounded evaluation over generic performance.
